summary: The repaired BindingThermo.lean reaches ALL CHECKED on the first run: 9 theorems, 0 errors, 0 sorryAx, 9/9 axiom lines, each depending only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The statement of cheng_prusoff_binding is true as written and was not changed or weakened; only the proof was broken. I replaced the fragile `field_simp` / `first | ring | ...` chain with explicit cancellation lemmas and `linear_combination`. I did not re-run the old file to see exactly which tactic failed, so the cause is a reading of the proof, not a measurement: the last line's `first` could fall through to a bare `field_simp`, which can succeed without closing the goal. The other seven theorems are kept with identical statements; `half_occupancy_at_Kd` got a sturdier proof for the same reason. I added one new theorem, `cheng_prusoff_binding_unique` (the converse: a non-negative inhibitor concentration that halves occupancy must equal Ki*(1+L/Kd)), so the IC50 relation is now if-and-only-if inside the model. All docstrings were rewritten to say what each theorem shows and does not show. The negative control (a false 'IC50 = Ki' claim closed with sorry) is rejected by check.sh as required (sorryAx=1, FAILED). Lean runs used: 2 (one through check.sh via run.sh, one direct to capture the full axiom lines). Files are in D:/Users/ashenoy00000/delphi-work/agents5/lb-binding-thermo-fix/: BindingThermo.lean, BindingThermoNegativeControl.lean, run.sh, check_main.txt, check_negative.txt, axioms_full.txt. The repo was not edited; the failed copy is still in tracks/research/lean/failed/.

findings.claim: cheng_prusoff_binding is true as stated; the statement was left unchanged and now depends only on the three standard Mathlib axioms.

What was wrong was the proof, not the statement. With I = Ki(1+L/Kd) the denominator L + Kd(1 + I/Ki) equals 2(L+Kd), so occupancy is exactly half. The likely failure point is the final `first | ring | (field_simp; ring) | field_simp`, whose last branch can succeed while leaving the goal open; this was inferred from the source and STATE.md, not re-measured by re-running the old file.

suite.case_name: Binding thermodynamics (single-site binding, Cheng-Prusoff) - Lean repair
suite.statement: In the competitive single-site model, inhibitor at I = Ki*(1 + L/Kd) exactly halves labelled-ligand occupancy, and that is the only non-negative I that does so.
suite.validation: Kernel check through tracks/lean/check.sh: errors=0, sorryAx=0, axiom-lines=9/9. Negative control (false IC50 = Ki claim with sorry) is rejected. No comparison with experimental binding data was made in this task.
suite.holdout_set: Not applicable: pure algebra, no organism data used; nothing from the frozen holdout clade was read or written.
suite.performance: 9 of 9 theorems proved on the first check run; 2 Lean runs used of the 6 allowed.
suite.what_was_wrong: The statement was true; the proof was fragile. It relied on field_simp followed by `first | ring | ...` fallbacks, and the last fallback could succeed while leaving the goal open, which Lean records as sorryAx. Replaced with explicit cancellation lemmas and linear_combination. The exact failing tactic was inferred from reading the file, not confirmed by re-running the old version.

lay_summary: When a molecule sticks to a protein, a simple formula says what fraction of the protein is covered.
One proof about that formula, on how much of a blocking molecule cuts the coverage in half, had a gap, so the computer checker did not accept it.
The claim itself was right; only the written-out steps were sloppy, so I rewrote the steps and the checker now accepts all nine proofs.
I also proved the reverse: there is only one amount of blocker that cuts coverage exactly in half.
To make sure the checker is not just saying yes to everything, I gave it a wrong claim on purpose and it said no.

glossary.Kd: Dissociation constant: the free ligand concentration at which half the binding sites are filled. Smaller means tighter binding.
glossary.Ki: The same kind of constant for an inhibitor (the blocking molecule).
glossary.IC50: The inhibitor concentration that cuts the measured binding or activity in half.
glossary.Cheng-Prusoff relation: The formula linking IC50 to Ki: IC50 = Ki * (1 + L/Kd) for a competitive inhibitor.
glossary.occupancy: The fraction of binding sites that have a ligand on them.
glossary.competitive single-site binding: A model where ligand and inhibitor fight for the same one spot on the protein.
glossary.sorryAx: Lean's marker that a proof has a hole in it; a theorem that depends on it is not proved.
glossary.#print axioms: A Lean command listing the basic assumptions a proof rests on; it reveals hidden holes.
glossary.negative control: A deliberately wrong input used to confirm the checker can say no.
glossary.named hypothesis: A physical assumption written openly as an input to a theorem, instead of being hidden.
glossary.linear_combination: A Lean tactic that proves an equation by adding up multiples of equations already known.

recommendations: Replace tracks/research/lean/failed/hv-mol-binding-thermo__BindingThermo.lean with this file through integrate-fleet.sh (I did not touch the repo).
In other harvested Lean files, look for `first | ... | field_simp` endings: a bare field_simp as the last alternative can succeed without closing the goal, the same defect pattern.
These theorems are only model algebra. To make them a validation case, pair them with measured IC50/Ki/Kd triples (e.g. ChEMBL) and test whether IC50/Ki = 1 + L/Kd holds; that was not done here.

For the linker-biology biomaterial proposal, the occupancy and Cheng-Prusoff theorems apply only if the linker binds one site with free ligand in excess; multivalent linkers need an avidity model, which this file does not cover.
